findings.title: No safe way to apply the journald cap on the existing server: it only runs as part of a full bootstrap.sh, which the docs say not to re-run
findings.body:
`configure_journald` is only reachable through `main()` in bootstrap.sh, after `create_directories`, `set_permissions`, `configure_firewall` and `configure_smartd`. The function is idempotent on its own: `install -d` plus `cat >` overwrites the file with the same content. But bootstrap.sh as a whole is not safe to re-run on a host where it already ran. `set_permissions` does `chown -R $PUID:$PGID` and `chmod -R 755/775/750` over appdata and every `/mnt/data` user tree. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 says outright «Не «чинить» права запуском `scripts/bootstrap.sh` на заполненном дереве». It also tells the operator to only restart smartd for smartd changes, «**не** прогон `bootstrap.sh` целиком».

The server whose disk is filling has already been bootstrapped, so it stays uncapped until someone runs the whole bootstrap. The new docs make this worse. ENVIRONMENT.md:138 and the new CLAUDE.md block say only that «`bootstrap.sh` создаёт … 90-homelab.conf», with no instruction for an existing host. An agent following CLAUDE.md to apply the cap would run bootstrap.sh and recursively reset ownership and modes on the live data and appdata. Unlike the setup steps (`./scripts/setup/NN-*.sh` «любой шаг установки запускается отдельно»), this step cannot be run on its own. The recursive chown/chmod is pre-existing; the change makes it the only delivery path for this feature.
findings.fix: Move the journald drop-in into its own re-runnable step (e.g. `scripts/setup/NN-configure-journald.sh` sourcing config.sh), or let bootstrap.sh run just that function from an argument. Document in ENVIRONMENT.md/CLAUDE.md how to apply it on the existing host without running bootstrap.sh in full.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the dangling-image prune keeps the local rollback copy, but that copy is exactly what it deletes
findings.body:
The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.»

Here is what `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) does for a service on a moving tag such as `:latest`:
1. `compose pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes untagged, i.e. dangling.
2. `down` + `up -d` replaces the container that referenced the old image.
3. The new `docker image prune -f` (rebuild.sh:33) deletes that previous image, because it is now dangling and unused.

So after a rebuild that pulled a new image, no local previous version is left to roll back to. The worst case is a service whose `pull` and `down` succeed but whose `up -d` fails. The prune still runs, by design, and deletes the only local copy of the working old version.

The part about stopped services' images is correct: those stay tagged. The rollback claim is false. CLAUDE.md tells agents to read ENVIRONMENT.md before disk work, so an operator or agent may plan a rollback around an image that is gone. This is a documentation defect only.
findings.fix: Drop «и локальная копия для отката». Say that tagged images, including those of stopped services, are kept, but the previous version of an updated image is removed, so a rollback means pulling a pinned tag again.

findings.title: The disk-space push shows the free-space value without its unit
findings.body: Both new messages render `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.`. `states()` returns only the bare number. The unit (GiB for the Glances disk_free sensors) is an attribute and is not included. So the push reads e.g. "SSD: занято 87.3%, свободно 12.4." with no unit. The neighbouring alerts in this file write their unit into the template (`°C` at lines 92, 106, 123; `RPM` at 199), and the usage half of these same messages adds `%` by hand. The problem is on both line 64 (SSD) and line 78 (RAID).
findings.fix: Append the unit on both lines, e.g. `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} ГБ`, or use `state_attr(..., 'unit_of_measurement')`.

findings.title: Dashboard comment still says «Три группы» after a fourth group was added
findings.body: The comment just above the cards reads «# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance…». It described the old layout: Диски / Материнка / Вентиляторы. This change adds a fourth group, «Место», so the comment now gives the wrong count. The view header comment (lines 486-493) lists which sensors were added and when, but it does not mention the new rootfs usage sensors.
findings.fix: Change «Три группы» to «Четыре группы» (or drop the count), and note the rootfs usage sensors in the view header comment.

findings.title: config.sh is now sourced twice in bootstrap.sh; the source inside configure_network is dead
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top level (bootstrap.sh:66) so that `configure_journald` can read `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`. `configure_network` still sources the same file at line 197. config.sh only assigns and exports constants, and nothing between line 66 and line 197 changes them, so the second source has no effect. It also suggests the function needs its own private load, which is no longer true. The project's existing pattern is one top-level load, as in scripts/setup/06-run-bootstrap.sh:9.
findings.fix: Delete the `source` line inside `configure_network` (bootstrap.sh:197).

findings.title: The journald cap can only be applied by rerunning the full bootstrap, which the docs forbid on the live server
findings.body:
`configure_journald` is reachable only from `bootstrap.sh`'s `main()`. There is no separate `scripts/setup/NN-*.sh` step for it, and no documented manual command. The server is already set up, so the only way to get the drop-in onto it is to rerun `bootstrap.sh`. That also runs `set_permissions`: recursive `chown -R 1000:1000` / `chmod -R 775/750` over `/mnt/data/public`, `users`, `backups` and appdata. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 forbids exactly this ("Не «чинить» права запуском `scripts/bootstrap.sh` на заполненном дереве"), and KTD6 in the RAID plan calls it irreversible.

The new docs say only "`bootstrap.sh` создаёт `/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-homelab.conf`… и перезапускает `systemd-journald`" (ENVIRONMENT.md:138; same claim in CLAUDE.md:70). Meanwhile CLAUDE.md tells agents "любой шаг установки запускается отдельно". So either the cap never reaches the existing host, or an operator or agent applies it by running bootstrap and rewrites permissions on the whole data tree. The smartd section (ENVIRONMENT.md:163) shows the precedent for this situation: it documents the manual command and says not to run the whole of `bootstrap.sh`.
findings.fix: Document the manual application for an existing host in ENVIRONMENT.md/CLAUDE.md and repeat the warning against running the full bootstrap: write the two-line drop-in with `SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`, then `sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald`. Alternatively, move the step into its own standalone setup script.

findings.title: Claim that prune keeps the "local copy for rollback" is false: the previous image is the one that gets pruned
findings.body:
The doc says: "Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются." Services track reused tags such as `:latest`. When `do_rebuild` pulls a new image, the previous image loses its tag and becomes dangling. After `down`/`up -d` no container references it, so the `docker image prune -f` that `rebuild.sh` now runs deletes it.

This matters most when a service fails. If `up -d` fails after `pull` and `down` succeeded, the old image is dangling and unreferenced, and the prune (which deliberately runs after failures too) removes the only working previous version. The doc tells the operator a rollback copy survives; it does not.
findings.fix: Drop the rollback clause, or state that the previous version of a re-tagged image becomes dangling and is removed by the prune.

findings.title: Очистка не сохраняет локальный образ для отката
findings.body: Новое утверждение «локальная копия для отката остаётся» неверно при обновлении изменяемого тега. В do_rebuild команда pull переносит тег на новый образ, а down удаляет контейнер, который удерживал предыдущий образ. Если других тегов и контейнеров нет, предыдущий образ становится dangling и удаляется последующим docker image prune -f. Оператор не сможет выполнить обещанный локальный откат.
findings.fix: Указать, что предыдущий образ может быть удалён; для сохранения образа для отката нужен отдельный тег.

findings.title: The journald cap can only be applied by running all of bootstrap.sh, and the recursive set_permissions step runs before it
findings.body:
The new `configure_journald` step (defined around lines 414-426) is wired in only as the last step of `main()` in `scripts/bootstrap.sh`. There is no `scripts/setup/NN-*.sh` step for it and no documented manual command. The function itself is idempotent: `install -d` plus `cat >` overwrites the drop-in, then journald restarts. The only way to reach it, though, is a full bootstrap run, and that run is not safe on a host where bootstrap already ran.

The live server was bootstrapped before this change. Getting the cap onto it means rerunning bootstrap.sh in full, and that calls `set_permissions` first (lines 141-165): `chown -R 1000:1000` and `chmod -R 775/750` over `$APPDATA_PATH`, `$DATA_PATH/public`, `$DATA_PATH/users/*` and `$DATA_PATH/backups`. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 forbids exactly this: «Не «чинить» права запуском `scripts/bootstrap.sh` на заполненном дереве». chmod without `X` sets the exec bit on every file, and chown overwrites the `root:root` that Syncthing sets on purpose. A full rerun also redoes the netplan, firewall and docker-user steps first, so under `set -e` any failure in those stops the run before the journald step.

The new docs (ENVIRONMENT.md:138, CLAUDE.md:70) say only that «`bootstrap.sh` создаёт … 90-homelab.conf» and restarts journald. CLAUDE.md also says «любой шаг установки запускается отдельно», but this step cannot run on its own. That leaves two outcomes:
- Nobody reruns bootstrap, and the journal on the live SSD stays uncapped while the docs read as if the cap is in place.
- An operator or agent follows the docs, reruns bootstrap.sh, and permissions under appdata and /mnt/data get rewritten recursively.

The smartd section (ENVIRONMENT.md:163) shows the precedent for this situation: it documents the manual command and says not to run the whole of bootstrap.sh.
findings.fix: Make the journald configuration a standalone, re-runnable step (e.g. `scripts/setup/NN-setup-journald.sh` sourcing config.sh, or a `configure_journald`-only entry point that bootstrap also calls). In ENVIRONMENT.md/CLAUDE.md, document applying it on an existing host without the full bootstrap: write the drop-in with `SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`, then `sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald`.

findings.title: A disk alert is lost if automations reload during its 10-minute window, or if it is deployed while usage is already above the threshold
findings.body: numeric_state arms an entity at attach time only if the entity is currently below the threshold. So two cases lose the alert. First, an automation reload or HA restart during the 10-minute `for:` window, while usage is already above 85% (SSD, lines 54-59) or 90% (RAID, lines 68-73). Second, deploying these automations when a disk is already over the threshold. In both cases the alert will not fire until the value drops back below the threshold and crosses it again. Two things limit this. First, the entity re-arms whenever the sensor goes unavailable and comes back: a failed numeric check arms it, and the file's server_glances_autoreload notes say that happens after Glances restarts or the server reboots. Second, disk usage changes slowly, and every existing temperature alert in the file uses the same trigger pattern. So the gap is real but narrow, not 'never re-arms'.
findings.fix: Optionally add a `homeassistant: start` / `event: automation_reloaded` trigger with a numeric_state condition (above 85/90), so an exceedance that already exists still produces a push.

findings.title: New CLAUDE.md block and rebuild comment are in English inside a Russian instruction file
findings.body: Every other block of CLAUDE.md is in Russian, apart from the boilerplate `## Agent skills` section. The new block (lines 70–72, e.g. "`rebuild.sh` prunes dangling Docker images after all requested services, including a run where a service failed") and the edited comment on line 61 ("pull + restart, then prune dangling images", next to "остановка", "деплой") are in English. The mismatch changes no agent behaviour, but it breaks the file's convention, and the ENVIRONMENT.md version of the same facts was written in Russian.
findings.fix: Translate lines 61 and 70–72 into Russian so they match the surrounding blocks and ENVIRONMENT.md «Контроль свободного места».

findings.title: Disk-space push messages print the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: Both new messages render `свободно {{ states('sensor.…_disk_free') }}.` (line 64 for rootfs, line 78 for RAID). `states()` returns only the number. The unit (GiB from Glances) is in the `unit_of_measurement` attribute. The push reads like «SSD: занято 87.1%, свободно 31.4.», and the reader cannot tell GiB from GB or percent. Every other message in this file adds its unit by hand (`°C`, `%`). Only the free-space value has none.
findings.fix: Append the unit: `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} {{ state_attr('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free', 'unit_of_measurement') }}` (same for the RAID sensor), or hard-code ` GiB`/` ГиБ`.

findings.title: Disk-space alerts need a below-threshold reading first: a disk already over the threshold at deploy or reload, or a reload during the 10-minute `for:`, never alerts
findings.body: Both new automations (lines 55–59 for SSD, 69–73 for RAID) use a `numeric_state` trigger with `above: 85` / `above: 90` and `for: "00:10:00"`. In HA this trigger is armed only by a reading outside the range. At setup it arms the entity only if the current value is below the threshold. If the disk is already over 85% / 90% when the package is deployed, when automations are reloaded (any UI automation edit does this), or when HA restarts with Glances already up, the trigger never arms and never fires. A reload or restart inside the 10-minute `for:` window also cancels a pending alert, and the trigger then sets up again in the not-armed state. Disk usage rarely drops back down, so in these cases the alert can stay silent indefinitely. An earlier claim that crossings during Glances unavailability are lost is wrong: an armed trigger stays armed through an unavailable state, and that path still fires. The gap is limited to the deploy/reload/restart cases above. The dashboard group still shows the values.
findings.fix: Add a `homeassistant: start` trigger and a periodic `time_pattern` trigger (e.g. `hours: "/1"`, as `server_glances_autoreload` already does with `/10`). Then add a `numeric_state` condition above 85/90 with `for: "00:10:00"`. Keep `mode: single`. This only touches the two new automations.

findings.title: Doc claims the rollback copy of an image survives the prune; it is exactly what gets pruned
findings.body: The new ENVIRONMENT.md line says that after `rebuild.sh` runs `docker image prune -f`, 'Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются'. But `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) does `pull` → `down` → `up -d`. The pull moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image loses its tag. Once `up -d` recreates the container on the new image, nothing references the old one, so it is dangling, and that is what `docker image prune -f` deletes. After a rebuild, the previous version of a rebuilt service is gone from the host. Anyone reading this (ENVIRONMENT.md is the reference CLAUDE.md tells agents to read first) would expect an older local image to roll back to and would not find one.
findings.fix: Drop 'и локальная копия для отката' or say the reverse: the previous image of every rebuilt service is removed, so rolling back means pulling the old tag again.

findings.title: configure_network still re-sources config.sh, which bootstrap now loads at top level
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top level of bootstrap.sh (line 66) so that `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` is defined. `configure_network` still sources the same file again at line 197, and that call is now redundant. Bootstrap does not reassign any config.sh variable between the two. Two load points make it unclear which one matters, and future edits could make them diverge.
findings.fix: Delete the `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` line inside configure_network. The top-level source at line 66 already provides NET_IP, NET_INTERFACE_MATCH and the rest.

findings.title: Server view comment still says «Три группы» after a fourth group («Место») was added
findings.body: The comment above the Сервер view's cards reads «Три группы вместо одной плитки glance…». This change adds a new separator/grid group «Место» at the top of that card list, so the view now has four groups: Место, Диски, Материнка, Вентиляторы. The comment no longer matches the code below it.
findings.fix: Change to «Четыре группы…» (or drop the count) and mention that «Место» shows the rootfs disk-usage sensors.

findings.title: Server view comment still says «Три группы» after the change adds a fourth group
findings.body: The comment directly above the edited cards reads «Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: та выкладывала семь разнородных значений в общую сетку…». This change inserts a new separator group «Место» (line 503-505) at the top of that card list. The view now has four groups (Место, Диски, Материнка, Вентиляторы); before the change there were three. Read side by side, the comment and the new separator contradict each other. The comment is the one that is wrong.
findings.fix: Update the comment to «Четыре группы…» (or drop the count) and mention that «Место» shows the rootfs disk-usage sensors.

findings.title: Disk-space push messages show the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: Both new alerts write `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.` — `states()` returns only the numeric state, not `unit_of_measurement`. As far as I know (not checked against a live install), the Glances `disk_free` sensor reports in GiB, so the push reads like 'SSD: занято 87.2%, свободно 11.9.' and gives no unit for the number the alert exists to report. The usage part hardcodes `%` and is fine. Contained cosmetic impact on the notification text.
findings.fix: Append the unit, e.g. `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} {{ state_attr('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free', 'unit_of_measurement') }}` or a literal ` ГБ`.

findings.title: Applying the journald cap on a live server requires rerunning bootstrap, which first re-runs set_permissions on appdata and DATA_PATH
findings.body: On a server where bootstrap has already run, the only way to apply or re-apply the journald limit through this script is to run bootstrap again, and bootstrap calls set_permissions first. That function recursively changes owners and modes in appdata and DATA_PATH. ENVIRONMENT.md warns that this also overwrites Syncthing permissions. The permission step existed before this change, but the new step puts it on the path to configuring journald on a live server.
findings.fix: Make the journald configuration a separate step (for example its own setup/NN-*.sh) that can be rerun without running the rest of bootstrap.

findings.title: Таймер numeric_state не переживает перезапуск Home Assistant
findings.body: Если заполнение диска превысило порог, но Home Assistant перезапустился или автоматизации были перезагружены до истечения 10 минут, ожидающий таймер сбрасывается. Если датчик при загрузке уже показывает значение выше порога, новый переход через порог не происходит, и уведомление не отправится, пока заполнение не опустится ниже порога и снова не превысит его. Та же проблема есть у RAID-уведомления.
findings.fix: Добавить проверку сохраняющегося превышения при запуске и после перезагрузки автоматизаций, используя сохраняемое время или периодическую проверку.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the rollback copy survives the prune, but `docker image prune -f` deletes the pre-pull image of every rebuilt service
findings.body: The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.» `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) runs `pull` → `down` → `up -d`. The pull moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image is left untagged (`<none>:<none>`). Once the container is recreated on the new image, nothing references the old one. It is dangling, and the `docker image prune -f` added at rebuild.sh:33 deletes it. The same happens on the failed-service path, where `up -d` fails after a successful pull and down. Nothing in the repo tags the old image for rollback. After a rebuild there is no local copy to roll back to. CLAUDE.md tells agents to read ENVIRONMENT.md first, so an operator or agent who plans to restart the previous local image after a bad update will find it gone. The claim is also the stated reason the prune is considered safe. The part about tagged images of stopped services staying is correct.
findings.fix: Replace the rollback clause, e.g. «образы остановленных сервисов остаются; предыдущая версия образа пересобранного сервиса становится dangling и удаляется — откат только через повторный pull конкретного тега/digest». Alternatively, tag the old image before pulling if a local rollback copy is actually wanted.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md hard-codes the journal cap value instead of pointing to config.sh
findings.body: ENVIRONMENT.md:138 hard-codes `SystemMaxUse=1G`. CLAUDE.md names `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` in `scripts/lib/config.sh` as the source of this value, and bootstrap.sh reads it from there. If config.sh changes to 2G and bootstrap is rerun, the host gets 2G while ENVIRONMENT.md still says 1G. The alert thresholds (85%/90%) are likewise restated in CLAUDE.md, ENVIRONMENT.md and hardware_health.yaml.
findings.fix: Write «`SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` (scripts/lib/config.sh)» rather than the literal 1G. Optionally point the threshold lines at hardware_health.yaml.

findings.title: The new block's trigger "Home Assistant hardware alerts" is wider than its content
findings.body: The trigger `<important if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant hardware alerts">` also fires for any work on the CPU-temperature, fan and RAID-temperature alerts in hardware_health.yaml. The block itself only covers disk-usage alerts, so those runs load content that does not apply to them. Work on the «Сервер» dashboard's «Место» group, which line 72 describes, does not match the trigger wording at all. The branch is "disk usage alerts/dashboard", not "hardware alerts".
findings.fix: Narrow the trigger to the branch the block handles, e.g. `if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant disk-usage alerts or dashboard"`.

findings.title: Dashboard comment still says three groups after a fourth («Место») was added
findings.body: The comment directly above the cards still reads `# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: ...`. This change adds a «Место» separator and grid in front of «Диски», «Материнка» and «Вентиляторы», so the Сервер view now has four groups. The comment gives the wrong count for the layout it describes.
findings.fix: Change "Три группы" to "Четыре группы", or drop the count.

findings.title: Disk-space push shows the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: The SSD and RAID messages (lines 64 and 78) end with `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.`. `states()` returns only the bare number, without the sensor's unit (Glances reports disk free in GiB). The push therefore reads something like "свободно 12.3.". The other alerts in this file always add the unit by hand, for example `°C` at lines 89 and 104, and these messages do the same for usage with `%`. The free-space value is the only one left without a unit.
findings.fix: Add the unit after the template, e.g. `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} ГБ.`, and do the same for the RAID message.

findings.title: configure_network still sources config.sh, which bootstrap now sources at the top level
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top level (line 66) so `configure_journald` can read `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`. That load already supplies the `NET_*` values that configure_network reads, so the second `source` at line 197 now does nothing. Nothing between the two loads changes those variables. The extra line makes it look as if config is loaded only inside that function, or as if it overrides something, and neither is true. The line predates this change, but this change made it dead.
findings.fix: Delete the `source` line inside `configure_network` (scripts/bootstrap.sh:197).

findings.title: rebuild.sh header still says only "pull + restart" after the change adds an image prune
findings.body: The change updates the usage lines in README.md and CLAUDE.md to "pull + restart, then prune dangling images". The script's own header was not updated: `# Rebuild Docker Services (pull + restart)`. Someone who reads the script, or runs it directly on the server, gets no hint that every run, including one where a service failed, now deletes dangling images host-wide, not just for the services named.
findings.fix: Change the header to `# Rebuild Docker Services (pull + restart, then prune dangling images)`.

findings.title: Journald cap only applies through a full bootstrap.sh run, whose set_permissions must not be rerun on the populated host
findings.body: `configure_journald` is called only from bootstrap.sh `main()`. There is no standalone entry point or argument to run it alone. `main()` also runs `set_permissions`, which does recursive `chown -R` and `chmod -R` over appdata, `$DATA_PATH/public`, users and backups. The project already documents this as irreversible on a populated tree (ENVIRONMENT.md:176, the RAID1 migration plan KTD6; ENVIRONMENT.md:163 says to restart smartd by hand rather than rerun bootstrap.sh). The function itself is idempotent, but the docs (ENVIRONMENT.md:138, CLAUDE.md:70) give no safe way to apply it on the existing server. So either the cap never reaches the live host, or the operator reruns bootstrap and rewrites ownership and modes across appdata and the RAID tree.
findings.fix: Move configure_journald into its own setup step (e.g. scripts/setup/NN-configure-journald.sh sourcing config.sh), or let bootstrap.sh run a single step by argument. Document that command, not a bootstrap rerun, in ENVIRONMENT.md and CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: Disk-space alerts are lost if HA restarts/reloads while usage is already above the threshold but before the 10-minute alert has fired
findings.body: HA's numeric_state trigger only arms an entity whose value is below the threshold when the trigger attaches. A restart or automation reload cancels a pending `for:` timer. If that happens after usage has crossed 85% (SSD) or 90% (RAID) but before the 10-minute alert has fired, or if usage crosses the threshold while HA is down (for example during a homeassistant rebuild), the trigger stays disarmed. No push arrives until usage drops below the threshold and crosses it again. For a slowly filling disk that may never happen. The window is narrow, and every existing numeric_state alert in hardware_health.yaml has the same behaviour. The file already notes this transition-only pitfall for server_glances_autoreload. So this is a real but low-probability gap, not a major defect.
findings.fix: Add a `homeassistant: start` trigger (or the same `time_pattern` approach server_glances_autoreload uses) with a numeric_state condition `above: 85` / `above: 90`. That way a threshold that is already exceeded still produces a push.

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранение локального образа для отката
findings.body: При обновлении изменяемого тега, например homeassistant:stable, pull переносит тег на новый образ, а down удаляет контейнер со ссылкой на старый. Если других тегов и контейнеров нет, старый образ становится dangling и добавленный prune удаляет его. Поэтому локальная копия для отката не гарантирована, вопреки новой строке документации. Условия удаления подтверждает [документация Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/).
findings.fix: Убрать обещание сохранения копии для отката и указать, что предыдущий образ может быть удалён.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback image survives the prune, but the prune deletes it
findings.body: Line 139 says: "Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются." `do_rebuild` (`scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274`) runs `pull`, then `down`, then `up -d`. Almost every service uses a moving tag (`latest`, `stable`, `latest-full`, ...). The pull moves the tag to the new image, so the old image becomes `<none>:<none>`. Once `down`/`up -d` replace the container, nothing references the old image, so the new `docker image prune -f` in `rebuild.sh:33` deletes it. The failure path is affected too: if `down` succeeds and `up -d` fails, the last working image is pruned. After a rebuild there is no local copy to roll back to. ENVIRONMENT.md is agent-facing reference (CLAUDE.md:9), so an agent or operator would treat a rebuild as locally reversible when it is not. The script does what was intended; the defect is in the doc.
findings.fix: Replace the claim, e.g.: «Удаляются только dangling images, включая предыдущую версию образа обновлённого сервиса — локального отката после rebuild нет; образы остановленных сервисов (с тегом) остаются.» Optionally add that a rollback copy needs a tag or digest pin before rebuilding.

findings.title: Journald cap can only reach the already-running server by re-running bootstrap.sh, which ENVIRONMENT.md forbids there
findings.body: `configure_journald` is reachable only through `main()` in scripts/bootstrap.sh (line 464). It runs after `set_permissions`, which does `chown -R 1000:1000` and `chmod -R 775/750` over appdata and /mnt/data/{public,users,backups}. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 explicitly says not to run bootstrap.sh on the populated tree. For the analogous smartd change, ENVIRONMENT.md:163 documents a targeted command instead of re-running bootstrap. The new journald docs (ENVIRONMENT.md:138, CLAUDE.md:71) only say that `bootstrap.sh` creates the drop-in and give no way to apply it to the already-running server. The live server is the only host and the target of issue #8. The most likely outcome is that its SSD stays uncapped. The alternative is someone re-running bootstrap and damaging permissions on the data tree.
findings.fix: In ENVIRONMENT.md «Контроль свободного места», document a one-off apply for the existing host, for example: `sudo install -d /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d && printf '[Journal]\nSystemMaxUse=1G\n' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-homelab.conf && sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald`. Add a note to not re-run bootstrap.sh for this, matching the smartd note. Optionally move the logic into a standalone scripts/setup/NN-*.sh step.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback copy survives the prune, but the prune deletes it
findings.body: Line 139 says that after `docker image prune -f` "образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются". Most services use moving tags (`latest`, `stable`, `beta`, or no tag). `do_rebuild` runs `compose pull`, then `down`, then `up -d`. The pull moves the tag to the new image, which leaves the previous image untagged. Once the container is replaced, nothing references it. That makes it exactly the dangling image the new prune in rebuild.sh:33 deletes, including when `up -d` fails after `down`. Nothing in the repo re-tags or keeps old images. An operator or agent who trusts this sentence will plan a rollback around a local image that no longer exists. Only the prose is wrong; the script does what the goal specifies.
findings.fix: Drop the 'локальная копия для отката' clause, or state that the prune removes the previous (now untagged) version of a rebuilt image, so a rollback needs a registry pull of a specific tag.

findings.title: Disk-space push messages print free space as a bare number with no unit
findings.body: Both new messages interpolate `states('sensor.…_disk_free')`, which returns only the bare number. The unit (GiB) is in a separate attribute. The push therefore reads, for example, "SSD: занято 87.3%, свободно 41.2." with no unit on the free value. Every other message in this file writes its unit out (`°C`, `RPM`, and `%` for usage here).
findings.fix: Append the unit, e.g. `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} ГБ`, or use `state_attr(..., 'unit_of_measurement')`. Do the same in the RAID message.

findings.title: Dashboard comment still says three groups after a fourth («Место») was added
findings.body: The comment heading the «Сервер» view cards reads "Три группы вместо одной плитки glance…". This change adds a fourth separator group, «Место», above «Диски», «Материнка» and «Вентиляторы», so the comment now describes the old layout.
findings.fix: Change "Три группы" to "Четыре группы", or drop the count.

findings.title: Disk-space alert can be missed for good if HA restarts or reloads around the threshold crossing
findings.body: HA's `numeric_state` trigger fires only when an entity moves from 'not matching' to 'matching'. The trigger is armed at the moment the automation attaches. If HA restarts or automations reload during the 10-minute `for` window, the pending timer is dropped. Once Glances is loaded and already reports usage above 85%, the trigger is not re-armed. The same happens if HA was down when the crossing occurred. Disk usage only climbs, so it rarely drops back under the threshold to cross it again, and the SSD can fill with no push. A Glances unavailable→value blip does re-arm the trigger, which softens this somewhat. The window is narrow, so this is minor, but it weakens the guarantee CLAUDE.md documents (alert above 85%/90%). The RAID automation (lines 70–73) has the same problem.
findings.fix: Add a `platform: homeassistant, event: start` trigger (and optionally a periodic `time_pattern`), plus a `numeric_state` condition with `above: 85` (90 for RAID) and `for: 00:10:00`, so a value already above the threshold still fires. The change stays inside the two new automations.

findings.title: configure_network still sources config.sh, now redundant after the new top-level source
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at script scope (line 66), so all config variables are loaded before `main` runs. The existing `source` inside `configure_network` (line 197) now only re-runs config.sh. That leaves two places loading the same configuration, and a reader can't tell which one is authoritative. Runtime behaviour is unaffected.
findings.fix: Remove the `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` line inside `configure_network`.

findings.title: Шаг journald прерывает установку в тестовом контейнере
findings.body: При запуске установки с TEST_MODE=1 из tests/Dockerfile этот шаг всё равно вызывает systemctl restart systemd-journald. В контейнере без запущенного systemd команда завершается с ошибкой, а set -e прерывает bootstrap и установку. Соседние шаги, которым нужен systemd, например configure_smartd в scripts/bootstrap.sh:347, пропускаются в TEST_MODE.
findings.fix: Пропустить настройку journald в TEST_MODE, как другие шаги, зависящие от systemd.

findings.title: Документация обещает сохранить образ для отката
findings.body: При обновлении тега старый образ может стать dangling. После пересоздания контейнера он больше не используется, поэтому docker image prune -f удалит его. Утверждение, что локальная копия для отката остаётся, может привести оператора к попытке отката на уже удалённый образ.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что dangling-версия предыдущего образа может быть удалена.

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранить образ для отката
findings.body: После обновления тега старый образ может стать dangling, если контейнер больше его не использует. Команда `docker image prune -f` удалит такой образ, поэтому локальная копия для отката не обязательно останется.
findings.fix: Указать, что предыдущий образ может быть удалён, если он стал dangling.

findings.title: Таймер предупреждения сбрасывается при перезапуске Home Assistant
findings.body: Если диск превысил порог и Home Assistant перезапустился или автоматизации были перезагружены до истечения 10 минут, таймер `for` сбрасывается. После перезапуска `numeric_state` ждёт нового пересечения порога: если заполнение остаётся выше 85%, предупреждение не придёт, пока значение сначала не опустится ниже порога и не превысит его снова. То же относится к RAID на строках 70–73.
findings.fix: Добавить проверку сохраняющегося превышения после запуска или перезагрузки автоматизаций, сохранив задержку в 10 минут.

findings.title: The block's trigger "Home Assistant hardware alerts" covers more than its content
findings.body: The trigger is `<important if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant hardware alerts">`. `hardware_health.yaml` also holds the CPU temperature and fan alerts, so this block fires whenever an agent edits any of those. Its content is only about disk usage. The extra branch makes the block load into context on work it has nothing to say about, and "Home Assistant hardware alerts" largely overlaps the existing `disk health, SMART` trigger. This changes no behaviour; it only adds context load.
findings.fix: Narrow the trigger to the branch the content serves, e.g. `if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant disk-usage alerts"`.

findings.title: Disk-space alert messages print the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: Both new alert messages write `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.`, once for rootfs and once for `..._mnt_data_disk_free` in the RAID alert. `states()` returns only the bare number (Glances reports disk_free in GiB), so the push reads like «SSD: занято 87.3%, свободно 12.4.» and the reader can't tell whether 12.4 means GB, GiB or percent. The usage half of the same message has a hard-coded `%`, and every other message in this file writes a unit after `states()` (`°C`).
findings.fix: Add the unit after the template, e.g. `свободно {{ states('...disk_free') }} GiB.`, or append `{{ state_attr('...disk_free','unit_of_measurement') }}`.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md claims dangling-only prune keeps a local rollback copy; it deletes exactly that image
findings.body: The new line says `docker image prune -f` removes only dangling images and that the local rollback copy stays ("локальная копия для отката остаются"). In `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh), `pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image loses its tag. Then `down` / `up -d` remove the only container that used it, so it is dangling when rebuild.sh:33 prunes, and the prune deletes it. Issue #8, the spec for this change, says so directly: "Dangling-only does not keep a rollback copy either: after `pull`, the previous `:latest` image loses its tag and is pruned." The worst case is a rebuild where `up -d` fails after `down` has succeeded: the operator reads this doc, expects to start the old image again, and finds it was deleted in the same run. The goal requires that ENVIRONMENT.md says what the scripts do.
findings.fix: Replace the claim with: «образы остановленных сервисов остаются; предыдущая версия пересобранного образа после pull становится dangling и удаляется — локальной копии для отката нет».

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says rebuild keeps a local rollback copy, but the prune deletes the previous image
findings.body: The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.» (only dangling images are removed; images of stopped services and the local rollback copy stay). That is not what happens. `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:193-195) runs `compose pull`, which moves the tag to the new image and leaves the old image untagged. `down` then removes the container that used the old image, and `up -d` starts a new one from the new image. By the time `docker image prune -f` runs (rebuild.sh:33), the old image is dangling and nothing uses it, so the prune deletes it. That old image is the one you would roll back to. An operator who trusts this sentence and tries to return a service to the old image after a bad update will find it gone and will have to pull an older tag from the registry. This is prose, so it is minor. The part about stopped services is correct, because tagged images are kept.
findings.fix: Replace the rollback claim with something like: «предыдущая версия образа после pull становится dangling и тоже удаляется — откат только через pull конкретного тега» (the previous image becomes dangling after pull and is also deleted; rolling back means pulling a specific tag).

findings.title: Dashboard comment still says «Три группы» after the change adds a fourth group («Место»)
findings.body: The comment above the Сервер view's cards reads «Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: …». This change adds a new «Место» separator and grid right under that comment, ahead of «Диски», «Материнка» and «Вентиляторы». The view now has four groups, so the comment describes the layout as it was before the change. This affects the comment only; it has no runtime effect.
findings.fix: Change «Три группы» to «Четыре группы» (or drop the count).

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранить локальный образ для отката
findings.body: После обновления сервиса с тегом latest предыдущий образ теряет тег. В do_rebuild команда compose down удаляет старый контейнер, а compose up создаёт контейнер из нового образа. Если других ссылок на предыдущий образ нет, последующий docker image prune -f удаляет его. Поэтому добавленная гарантия сохранения локальной копии для отката неверна: оператор может рассчитывать на образ, которого после rebuild уже нет.
findings.fix: Уберите обещание сохранения копии для отката. Укажите, что предыдущий образ без тега и ссылок из контейнеров будет удалён.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback copy survives the prune, but the prune deletes that image
findings.body: The new line in ENVIRONMENT.md says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.» (only dangling images are removed; the local rollback copy stays). That is not what happens. `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh) runs `compose pull`, then `down`, then `up -d`. For a floating tag such as `:latest` or `homeassistant:stable`, the pull moves the tag to the new image and leaves the previous image untagged. Once the container is recreated, nothing uses the old image, so it is dangling. The `docker image prune -f` this change adds to rebuild.sh deletes exactly that image. Nothing in the repo tags a pre-rebuild image for rollback, and issue #8 itself notes that dangling-only pruning keeps no rollback copy. Worst case: `up -d` fails after `down` succeeded, and the same run deletes the only local copy of the last working image. CLAUDE.md tells agents to read ENVIRONMENT.md before disk work, so an operator or agent may plan a rollback around an image that no longer exists. The part about stopped services' tagged images is correct.
findings.fix: Replace the rollback clause with the real behaviour, e.g. «образы остановленных сервисов остаются; предыдущая версия пересобранного образа после pull становится dangling и удаляется — откат только через повторный pull старого тега/digest».

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md hard-codes SystemMaxUse=1G while CLAUDE.md names config.sh as the source
findings.body: `ENVIRONMENT.md` says bootstrap writes "`SystemMaxUse=1G`". `CLAUDE.md:70` correctly says the value is `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` in `scripts/lib/config.sh`. If `config.sh` changes, `ENVIRONMENT.md` will state a size the drop-in no longer has, and the two documents will disagree.
findings.fix: Write «`SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` (см. `scripts/lib/config.sh`, сейчас 1G)» or drop the literal value.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback copy of an image survives the dangling prune, but that copy is exactly what gets pruned
findings.body: The new line says that after `docker image prune -f` «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются». `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) runs `compose pull`, then `down`, then `up -d`, and the prune in scripts/docker/rebuild.sh:33 runs after that. Every service uses a mutable tag (`:latest`, `:stable`, `redis:8.4`, …). When `pull` fetches a newer image the tag moves, and the previous image becomes `<none>:<none>`. After `down` + `up -d` no container references it, so it is dangling and unused, and the prune deletes it. This also happens when `up -d` fails after `down`. Nothing in the repo retags images for rollback. An operator who expects to fall back to the previous local image after a bad update will find it gone. The part about stopped services' images is correct, because tagged images are not dangling.
findings.fix: Drop «и локальная копия для отката» and say what actually happens: the previous image of each rebuilt service becomes dangling after pull and is removed. To keep a fallback, tag it by hand first (e.g. `docker tag :rollback`) or pull again by digest.

findings.title: Numeric-state disk alerts lose their pending `for` timer on HA restart or automation reload
findings.body: Both new disk alerts (lines 55-59 and 69-73) use only a numeric_state trigger with `for: 00:10:00`. On a Home Assistant restart or automation reload, HA drops a pending `for` timer. HA also does not arm the trigger for an entity whose value is already above the threshold when the trigger attaches. Usage that crossed 85%/90% while HA was down, or during the 10-minute pending window, therefore never sends an alert. Disk usage changes slowly and can stay above the limit for days, so the safeguard stays silent until usage drops below the threshold and rises again. The window is narrow: once an alert has fired, a later restart loses nothing.
findings.fix: Add a `homeassistant: start` trigger (and/or a `time_pattern` hourly tick). Add a `numeric_state` condition with the same `above:` value so it alerts when usage is already over the threshold.

findings.title: Applying the journald cap on an existing server means re-running the full bootstrap, and that is unsafe
findings.body: The new journald step only runs after the other bootstrap steps. When bootstrap runs again on a server that is already set up, set_permissions first changes owner and mode recursively across appdata and the data directories. ENVIRONMENT.md (~line 176) warns that this overwrites Syncthing's deliberate permissions and adds the execute bit to files. The destructive behaviour was already there, but this change makes a full re-run of bootstrap the only way to apply the new setting.
findings.fix: Make journald configuration a separate step that can run on its own without set_permissions or the other bootstrap actions.

findings.title: Disk-space push messages print the free-space number with no unit
findings.body: Both new alert messages insert `{{ states('sensor.…_disk_free') }}` directly: line 64 for rootfs and line 78 for /mnt/data. `states()` returns only the number, without `unit_of_measurement`, and Glances reports disk_free in GiB. The push therefore reads «свободно 12.3.», and the reader cannot tell the unit. The neighbouring messages in the same file add their unit by hand (for example `°C`).
findings.fix: Add the unit, e.g. `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} GiB.` (same for RAID), or read it with `state_attr(..., 'unit_of_measurement')`.

findings.title: configure_network still sources config.sh, which bootstrap.sh now loads at the top
findings.body: The change adds a top-level `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` (line 66) so that `configure_journald` can read `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`. The older `source` inside `configure_network` (line 197) is now redundant and re-runs the same exports partway through. The two loads make it unclear which one bootstrap relies on. Someone who later deletes the top-level line, reasoning that configure_network sources it anyway, would leave `configure_journald` writing an empty `SystemMaxUse=`. Removing the inner line keeps behaviour the same, because nothing between line 66 and configure_network reassigns any config.sh variable.
findings.fix: Delete the `source` line inside `configure_network` (line 197).

findings.title: Server-view comment still says "three groups" after the change adds a fourth
findings.body: The comment above the new «Место» separator reads `# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: ...`. This change adds the «Место» group, so the Server view now has four groups: Место, Диски, Материнка, Вентиляторы. The comment describes the old layout and is stale.
findings.fix: Change «Три группы» to «Четыре группы», or drop the count.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the rollback copy of an image survives the prune, but the prune deletes it
findings.body: The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются». That is not what happens. `do_rebuild` runs `compose pull`, then `down`, then `up -d` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274). When the pull moves a tag to a new image, the previous image loses its tag (`<none>:<none>`). After `down` + `up -d` no container uses it, so it is dangling and unused, and the `docker image prune -f` added at scripts/docker/rebuild.sh:33 deletes it. Nothing in the repo keeps a separate rollback copy (no retag, no pinned previous digest; grep for откат/rollback finds nothing for images). An operator who reads this note and plans to fall back to the previous local image after a bad update will find it is gone and must pull it again by digest. The part about stopped services' images is correct, because tagged images are not dangling.
findings.fix: Drop the rollback claim and say the opposite: «Предыдущая версия образа после pull становится dangling и тоже удаляется — откат только повторным pull по тегу/digest».

findings.title: Комментарий к панели называет неверное число групп
findings.body: Комментарий на строке 499 говорит «Три группы», но добавленная группа «Место» делает их четырьмя. Комментарий описывает прежнее состояние панели и требует обновления.
findings.fix: Обновить число групп в комментарии или убрать его.

findings.title: Numeric-state triggers lose their pending timer on reload
findings.body: Если Home Assistant перезапустится или автоматизации будут перезагружены, пока диск уже заполнен выше порога, отсчёт `for` сбросится. Триггер ожидает нового пересечения порога, поэтому диск может оставаться переполненным без уведомления до тех пор, пока значение не опустится ниже порога и не поднимется снова. То же относится к RAID на строке 70.
findings.fix: Добавить проверку при запуске и после перезагрузки автоматизаций, которая учитывает длительность текущего состояния выше порога.

findings.title: Применение настройки журнала требует повторного полного bootstrap
findings.body: На уже настроенном сервере новый шаг доступен через полный запуск bootstrap. До него `set_permissions` рекурсивно меняет владельцев и права файлов в appdata и данных. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 прямо предупреждает, что это портит права Syncthing и добавляет бит исполнения файлам. Опасное поведение существовало раньше, но это изменение предлагает повторный bootstrap для применения новой настройки.
findings.fix: Вынести настройку journald в отдельно запускаемый шаг, который не выполняет остальные действия bootstrap.

findings.title: No test covers a service failure and a prune failure in the same rebuild run
findings.body: The service-failure test runs with a prune that succeeds, and the prune-failure test uses only services that succeed. If a change made the prune-error path clear the `failed` array, both tests would stay green, yet a run where both a service and the prune fail would make rebuild exit 0 instead of 1.
findings.fix: Add a scenario where both pull and prune fail in one run, and assert exit code 1 plus the prune warning.

findings.title: Prune-failure test accepts any `[!]` warning, not specifically the prune error
findings.body: The test checks only for the `[!]` marker. If the prune error message were replaced by any other warning with that marker, the test would stay green, while the operator would not learn that the dangling-image cleanup failed.
findings.fix: Assert that the warning text mentions the failed dangling-image cleanup.

findings.title: New block's trigger pulls in unrelated hardware-alert work and overlaps the existing disk-health and /mnt/data blocks
findings.body: The new pointer reads `<important if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant hardware alerts">`. Its body covers only the two disk-usage alerts. `hardware_health.yaml` also holds the CPU, NVMe, GPU and fan alerts. An agent editing a CPU temperature alert matches the 'Home Assistant hardware alerts' branch and loads the journald and prune bullets, which do not apply to that task. 'disk space' also sits right next to the existing `checking disk health, SMART, NVMe` trigger (line 128) and the `/mnt/data, the RAID array` trigger (line 135). On a task about RAID fill level, two or three blocks fire and the reader has to merge them. The skill's 'one trigger per branch' rule asks for a narrower branch name, such as 'disk usage alerts'. No wrong action follows from this; it is extra context load and a fuzzy trigger.
findings.fix: Narrow the third branch to the content, for example `<important if="you are working with disk space, journald, or disk-usage alerts">`.
